description:
Investigation only; no application code changed or runtime tests run. Current working tree inspected, including existing uncommitted storage changes.

Mental model / ownership: ZAQ selects enabled connectors, owns canonical identity/history and application storage integration, and supervises adapter listeners. jido_chat_whatsapp owns transport/protocol behavior. Amarula owns registries and per-connection trees. ZAQ config/config.exs directly configures [Amarula.Supervisor]; Channels.Supervisor.init inserts it before BridgeSupervisor using rest_for_one. mix.exs already uses ../jido_chat_whatsapp.

Flow / contracts: Adapter.listener_child_specs/2 returns ConnectionWorker only. Worker.init -> connect -> relay establish -> transport.connect; it never calls ensure_started. Package mix.exs and Amarula mix.exs have no Application mod callback. Pairing.run separately invokes transport.ensure_started; AmarulaClient.ensure_started -> start_supervisor calls Amarula.Supervisor.start_link from the caller. Removing host configuration alone therefore loses the normal listener prerequisite; lazy pairing startup is not a durable package supervisor owner.

State / invariants: One shared runtime per node, isolated profiles, no duplicate profile adoption, stopping one listener preserves storage and other profiles, stale instance cleanup must not stop a replacement. ZAQ RAM session storage must precede connector bootstrap. Current rest_for_one ordering restarts later bridges on shared runtime failure and preserves earlier limiter counters.

Risk: Worker relay monitors the listener owner, but no inspected monitor covers the shared runtime. Moving Amarula to a separate OTP application removes the host rest_for_one recovery coupling. Prove recovery of existing profiles on root, registry, and connections-supervisor failures, not just startup. Package application startup also occurs on non-Channels nodes unless designed otherwise; infrastructure can be idle there but must not open profiles. Host shutdown must still stop its connections without stopping other consumers.

Tests: ZAQ test/zaq/channels/supervision_test.exs covers parent shutdown, bridge reload, limiter preservation and shared-root failure, but hardcodes Amarula and currently expects three children despite the working-tree SessionStorage addition. Package storage_lifecycle_test.exs covers custom storage restore, duplicate owner rejection, stale cleanup, logout isolation, protocol process restart and reconnect; setup explicitly starts Amarula.Supervisor. Connection-worker tests cover attempt/profile isolation. These do not establish package-owned root recovery.

Unknowns / policy drift: package AGENTS.md says supervised runtime concerns belong in jido_messaging, while current package already implements host-supervised ConnectionWorker. Clarify transport infrastructure ownership versus host session orchestration in package guidance. Desired non-Channels-node startup policy and legacy host-supervised compatibility require explicit design in package work. No live WhatsApp behavior was tested.

Action reuse: not applicable to this read-only investigation. Proposed runtime work is local-only OTP lifecycle infrastructure, extending existing Transport/Adapter contracts rather than introducing business Actions or agent tools.

Recommendation: package-owned supervised shared transport runtime with reliable loss detection/recovery; then remove ZAQ Amarula configuration and concrete test dependencies. Merely replacing the config module with a wrapper hides the name but does not satisfy dependency-managed startup. Keep listener supervision and ZAQ storage integration at their existing boundaries.

Proposed delivery dependency: zaq-0l7.15 -> zaq-0l7.16.
```mermaid
graph LR
  package["zaq-0l7.15: package lifecycle"] --> host["zaq-0l7.16: ZAQ integration"]
```
title: [zaq-0l7.14] Investigate WhatsApp transport runtime ownership transition
